sun.upright:
Of all the knights in the deck, this is the one who never hurries. Look at his horse, head down, walking, and him holding the cup out in front like he's got the whole afternoon. For an Aries Sun that's an odd visitor. Aries is cardinal fire, ruled by Mars, and you know who you are by going first and going fast. The Knight is water. Fire and water are opposed elements, so before this card does anything else it tends to make you a bit itchy.

From the inside, it's the strange experience of being asked to want something softly. You know how to want things hard. You go after the job, the argument, the person, and you'd usually sooner lose than hang back. This card asks your will to turn up as an offer, a feeling held out where someone can take it or leave it, and that's more exposing for an Aries than people guess. You can't win an offer. You make it and then you wait, and waiting is the bit you're worst at. Your sign's own Major is The Emperor, who likes to decide how things end, and here the ending is in somebody else's hands.

At work it could be a project with your heart in it and your name on it, where you pitch it and the decision belongs to someone else. With a partner, or someone you're keen on, it's saying the tender thing straight, without turning it into a joke or a dare. It might be something creative you've kept to yourself because it isn't what people expect of you. Make the offer the way an Aries would, direct and out loud, and then leave it alone for a few days.
sun.reversed:
The chase is what gets you with this Knight upside down on an Aries Sun. You go after whoever or whatever is hardest to get, pour on the charm, and lose interest the week it works. Or the softness the card was asking for comes out as sulking, because Mars doesn't really know what to do with hurt except turn it into a fight, and a grand gesture that isn't answered quickly enough becomes a grudge you carry for months.

Dating shows it first, the thrill of the pursuit standing in for an actual person. At work it's the passion project you threw yourself at for a fortnight and left in a drawer the moment it stopped being new. You probably know which one I mean. Before you start anything else, go back to one thing you courted and dropped, and either finish it or tell the people involved plainly that you're out.

moon.upright:
Aries Moon feelings are quick. Something stings, you react, and ten minutes later it's done with and you've honestly forgotten what the fuss was about. Mars rules Aries, so even your emotional reflexes want to do something with what they feel. Then this card turns up carrying a slow, aching kind of feeling, one that doesn't want solving, and water and fire don't sit easily together. It'll probably feel like a mood you can't punch your way out of.

Often it's longing. Missing someone, wanting a thing you can't have yet, getting a lump in your throat at a song in the supermarket and being cross about it. The Aries instinct is to act on that immediately, send the message, book the flight, make it stop. The Knight lets his horse walk. The feeling he carries is meant to be carried for a while before it's handed over, and I'll be honest, that's hard for you. I'd still say it's worth trying.

In the body it can come out as restlessness in the evenings, or heat in your face when you think about the person. With a partner it's wanting to be close and then snapping, because closeness makes you feel exposed. Sleep may bring vivid dreams. Next time the soft feeling arrives, let it stay the whole evening without fixing anything, and see what it's turned into by morning.
moon.reversed:
Hurt comes out as heat on an Aries Moon, and with this Knight reversed there's a fair bit of hurt about. A small disappointment, a plan cancelled, a message answered with one word, lands far harder than it should, and you go straight to temper or to a sulk that's trying very hard to look like you don't care. The romance in the card turns moody. You want to be chased, and you won't say so.

Whoever's closest gets the brunt of it, a partner who can't work out what they did, a flatmate who hears the door go. Your body runs hot and tired at once, and sleep gets choppy. When you feel the flare, try saying the hurt part first, out loud, clumsily if you have to, the actual words that you're hurt. In my experience it takes the fuel out of the anger faster than anything.

rising.upright:
People expect Aries rising to come through the door at a run, and usually you do. This Knight drawn for your mask slows the entrance right down to a walk. Strangers meet someone surprisingly gentle, a bit romantic, a bit dreamy, and then every so often the Mars underneath flashes through, a blunt remark, a dare, and they don't quite know what to make of you. Water laid over fire never fully settles, and that's part of the appeal.

With Aries on the ascendant, the sign opposite, Libra, is on your seventh house, the house of the person across the table, and Libra belongs to Venus. You're often drawn to grace and charm in other people while you're all elbows yourself. With this card on the front of you, a bit of that Venus quality crosses over to your side for once. You may find people opening up faster than usual and telling you things, because you look like someone who'll hold carefully whatever they're given.

On a first date you'll be the one who brings flowers, or whatever the equivalent is, and means it. In a job interview you'll come across as someone who loves the work, which helps, as long as you've got the facts ready too. Meeting a partner's family, you'll win over the one everyone warned you was difficult. Let the slower pace stay longer than feels natural, and don't rush to fill a silence with a joke.
rising.reversed:
Charm on an Aries rising can tip into pushiness when the Knight turns over. You come in with the big compliment, the flirt, the generous offer, and it lands as too much too soon, so people take a step back and you push harder. Or it goes the other way and you wear a moody, wounded look that makes you seem much harder to approach than you are. Either way there's a bit of steam coming off the first impression.

New places bring it out, a party where you only know the host, the first week in a job, the opening message on a dating app that's either overwhelming or nothing at all. Pick the smaller version of whatever you were about to do. Say one kind thing and stop there, and let the other person come a step toward you.

sun.upright:
This Knight doesn't gallop, and neither do you, which is a good start. Taurus is fixed earth, ruled by Venus, and you build who you are out of things that last, a home you love, a skill in your hands, a few people you've kept for years. Water and earth are friendly elements. Each gives the other shape, and what grows between them comes up slowly and stays up. So when a card this romantic is drawn for a Taurus Sun, it usually finds somewhere to land.

The Knight brings the offer, the idea, the sweet talk. Your side of it is the follow-through he's famous for lacking. You're the one who asks whether the lovely plan has a date on it and who's paying, and romance needs that, whatever the poets say. The tension is gentler here than with most signs, though it's there. Being courted makes a Taurus want to stop and savour, and sometimes an offer needs an answer sooner than you'd like to give one. The Hierophant is Taurus' own Major, the card of doing things properly, and plenty of Taurus Suns won't let themselves enjoy something until it's official.

In love this might be a relationship ready to go up a step, keys swapped, a holiday booked. With creative work, the craft you've been quietly getting good at might want showing to someone. With money, beauty is worth paying for, within reason. Give one dream a physical form, a deposit, a date on the calendar, something you can actually hold.
sun.reversed:
A Taurus Sun can get very comfortable being courted. With this Knight upside down, the lovely offer sits on the table for months while you enjoy the attention and never quite say yes. Or you say yes to the fantasy of a thing, the dream house, the dream partner, and won't touch the version that's actually available. Stubbornness starts calling itself having standards. Sometimes it's simpler than that, and you're buying beautiful things to fill the space where a feeling should be.

Money gives it away, so look at the purchases that were really about wanting to be looked after. In creative work it's the piece you keep polishing so nobody has to see it. In a relationship it's holding out for a gesture you've never asked for. Ask for it, plainly and in words, the one thing you've been waiting for someone to guess.

moon.upright:
Soft bread, clean sheets, someone's hand on the back of your neck. A Taurus Moon calms down through the body, and with Venus ruling the sign it's a matter of pleasure as much as comfort. This Knight comes in carrying feeling, and earth and water get on, so the mood of the card sinks in the way rain sinks into a garden bed. You may find yourself unusually tender, easily moved, a bit sentimental about small things.

It's warm, slow weather inside, which suits you. There's a pull toward the everyday kind of romance, the dinner you cook for someone, the song you play twice in a row. The quiet catch is that the Knight is a traveller, always on his way somewhere, and a Taurus Moon doesn't enjoy being on the way. You want the arriving. So underneath the contentment you might feel wistful, a longing for someone or something that hasn't turned up yet, and not know what to do with it except have another biscuit.

At home it's a good stretch for making things nice, flowers, a new lamp, the spare room finally sorted. With a partner, touch matters more than usual and words matter a bit less. Your sleep may get deeper, or your dreams very romantic. Plan one slow evening around the senses, good food, music, no screens, and share it if there's someone to share it with.
moon.reversed:
Comfort turns into a hiding place when the Knight flips on a Taurus Moon. The longing is still there, so you soothe it the way you know, the extra serve, the new thing in the online basket, the afternoon under a blanket, and none of it touches the actual want. Or you hold on. An old love, an old flat, a friendship that's gone quiet, all kept warm in your head long after the other person stopped tending it.

The body shows it as heaviness, the kind of tired that sleep doesn't fix. With a partner it can look like possessiveness, wanting them home, wanting everything to stay exactly as it was. Say out loud what you actually miss or want. Then do one physical thing about it, a walk somewhere new, a phone call made standing up.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising already walks into a room the way this Knight's horse walks, calm, even-paced, in no hurry to prove anything. Put the card on your mask and the first impression gets warmer and a good deal more romantic. People take you for kind and a little old-fashioned, the sort who remembers birthdays, and they're usually right. Venus rules your chart, so it doesn't hurt that you tend to look good doing it.

With Taurus on the ascendant, Scorpio is opposite, on the seventh house, and Scorpio is one of the three water signs this card belongs to. That matters. The people you end up close to often feel things more intensely than you show, and with this card you're meeting that intensity with open hands. Earth and water get on, so there's little friction between the card and your manner. If anything the danger is that you'll be so pleasant nobody notices how much you mean it.

On a date you'll be good company and a touch too patient. In a job where you deal with the public, people will trust you on sight, which is useful when you've got something to offer them. Your style might soften, a better coat, something in a colour you'd normally walk past. Make the invitation yourself this time, and say what it's for.
rising.reversed:
The calm front goes passive on Taurus rising. You look lovely and give nothing away, so people leave pleased and unsure whether you liked them. Or you wait to be chosen. You stand at the edge of the room being pleasant, hoping somebody will come over, and nobody does, and you go home feeling overlooked and a bit stubborn about it.

With Scorpio across the chart, it can pull in someone who reads your stillness as a challenge and pushes. First meetings and the first weeks of anything suffer most. At work it's the idea you had in the meeting and let someone else say. At the next gathering, pick one person and go over to them first. Ask a real question, the kind with a story in the answer.

sun.upright:
Gemini's own Major is The Lovers, and that card is about choosing, one person or one path out of two, with your whole heart. So it's interesting when the Knight of Cups turns up for a Gemini Sun. Gemini is mutable air, ruled by Mercury, and you find out who you are by talking, reading, asking, trying things on. The Knight finds out by feeling. Water and air are neutral with each other, so the card neither helps you nor gets in your way. The two need introducing, and you're the one doing the introductions.

What you'll notice is how hard it is to say what you feel without dressing it up. You can explain a feeling beautifully, make it funny, turn it into a story for the group chat. The card asks for the plain, unguarded version, and that sits oddly in your mouth. There's also the Gemini habit of keeping two options warm, and this Knight is riding toward one. I've met plenty of Gemini Suns who are brilliant at romance on paper and go shy the moment it has to be said in person.

In writing, or any work with words, it can be a lovely card, putting some feeling into what's usually clever. With a sibling or a close friend there might be a conversation that goes deeper than the usual banter. In love, it's the message you've drafted four times. Write one sentence that says what you feel, with no joke in it, and send it or say it.
sun.reversed:
This is the Knight as a smooth talker, and on a Gemini Sun he can be very smooth indeed. The feeling drains out of the words, so you say lovely things you half mean, flirt with three people because it's fun, and promise more than you've thought through. Nobody's being deceived on purpose. You liked the sound of it when you said it.

It tends to turn up in messages first, long charming threads that don't go anywhere, and plans made at eleven at night that you can't face in the morning. Friends and partners start taking your warmth with a pinch of salt, and that stings more than you'd admit. Go a bit quiet. Say less, mean all of it, and follow up on the one promise from last week that's still hanging.

moon.upright:
There's a feeling in you that doesn't want to be talked about, and a Gemini Moon hasn't a clue what to do with that. Normally you sort your moods out by talking them through, texting a friend, reading about it, turning it over until it makes sense. Mercury rules Gemini, so the mind is how you get your feelings to settle. This Knight brings the wordless kind, longing, tenderness, a pull toward someone, and water and air have to be introduced before they'll do anything together.

You'll know it as a mood you can't explain. Wistful for no reason, moved by music, oddly sentimental about a friend from school. The Gemini reflex is to analyse it down into something smaller. That doesn't really work with this card, and the feeling tends to come back later, at night, stronger for having been pushed away. There's a lighter side too. You're lovely company like this, softer and funnier, and people who normally get only your quick side get the rest of you.

Sleep is where it shows, the busy mind replaying conversations and inventing new ones. A brother or sister might ring for a sweet, nostalgic chat out of nowhere. With a partner you may want more reassurance in words than you usually need. Put on some music with no lyrics and let the feeling run for one whole piece before you try to name it.
moon.reversed:
Moods can swing by the hour for a Gemini Moon under this reversed Knight. You're mad about someone at lunch and bored of them by dinner, or you're caught up in a crush that's mostly made of messages, reading and rereading them, building a whole person out of punctuation. The feelings are real enough. They just don't stay still long enough to tell you anything.

Your phone shows it, the anxious checking, the reply you need to arrive. So does the night, when your head won't switch off. Friends may have noticed you running hot and cold with them. Write the feeling down by hand on paper, which is slower than a screen, and read it back the next day before you act on it or send anything.

rising.upright:
Quick-witted, curious, asking questions before they've finished saying their name. That's Gemini rising, with Mercury running the chart, so the first impression is nearly always about talk. Drawn as your mask, the Knight adds charm with some softness in it. You come across as clever and romantic at once, the person who makes a stranger laugh and then says something sweet enough to catch them off guard. The elements neither fight nor help, so it's a mix you have to put together fresh each time, and you usually manage it.

The sign opposite yours, Sagittarius, is on your seventh house, and it's fire, which water doesn't get on with. So the people you're drawn to, bold, blunt, adventurous, may not quite know what to do with the tender version of you that's on show. Some will love it. Others will think you're flirting when you're only being nice, and to be honest, sometimes you are flirting and pretending you're only being nice.

At parties and work events you'll be popular and a little mysterious. In any job that involves writing or selling, you'll persuade people by making them feel something. On first dates you'll be very good at the talking part. Let one conversation go long and personal, and resist the urge to move on to the next person.
rising.reversed:
Too smooth is the risk here. You tell people what they'd like to hear, and it comes so easily to a Gemini rising that you barely notice you're doing it. Strangers leave charmed and a bit uncertain, as though they've been talking to their own reflection. Some pick up on it straight away and trust you less for it.

At work it's the pitch that promised more than the product could do, and a new manager who likes you in the first meeting and wonders about you by the third. Socially it's the friend you said you'd ring and didn't, and on dating apps it's the witty opener you've sent to six people. Keep first impressions a bit plainer. Say one true thing about yourself early, even something small, so people have a real person to hold on to.

sun.upright:
Cancer is one of the three water signs this Knight comes out of, so with a Cancer Sun the card is speaking your own language. It's cardinal water, ruled by the Moon, and people forget the cardinal bit. You do start things. You start them by caring, by feeding people, making a home, being the one who rings. The Knight is that same impulse on horseback, feeling that sets out to find someone. The same element amplifies, which is lovely and also quite a lot.

The Chariot is Cancer's own Major, a rider boxed in by armour and a canopy, and the Knight is a rider too, only with the cup held out in front where anyone can see it. That's what you'll feel. The card asks you to be more openly tender than your shell usually allows, and it's frightening. It also puts your sense of purpose squarely in your relationships, which feels right until you notice you're giving so much that nobody gets a chance to give back. With two lots of water stacked up, it's easy to mistake feeling everything for doing something.

With family it might be an offer of peace, or of help, to someone you've been keeping at arm's length. In love it's a proposal of some sort, maybe a ring, maybe just a plan to share more of your lives. At home you'll want to host, cook, fill the table. Make one of those offers, and then let someone make one back to you and accept it without arguing.
sun.reversed:
Up comes the shell, and the tenderness turns into something harder to read. Moods. Silences meant to be noticed. Being hurt and waiting for someone to come and find you, then resenting it when they don't. For a Cancer Sun it's often nostalgia doing the damage, an old love or an old version of the family that everyone since has been measured against.

It shows most at home and with whoever you mother, in whatever form that takes. You give and keep a quiet tally. At work it can look like taking one bit of criticism personally for a week. A partner might feel they're being tested without being told the rules. Tell someone directly what you need from them, in one sentence, even if it feels childish, and let them have a go at giving it to you.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon has feelings that are deep and tidal and tied up with home and memory, and this Knight pours in more of the same. Cancer is inside his own territory. Water on water means you'll feel things at full strength, and I'd expect some tears at odd moments, at an ad, at an old photo, at a stranger being kind to you in a shop.

Most of it is good. The card brings a tender mood, a wish to look after and be looked after, a longing for someone to turn up at the door with soup. What makes it tricky is that the Knight is always a bit ahead of himself, riding toward a feeling that hasn't arrived. Under his influence a Cancer Moon can start missing things before they've ended, or feel homesick in its own kitchen. Being cardinal, you'll want to do something about it, and that something is usually looking after someone else so you don't have to sit with your own need.

At home it's a good time to cook the thing your grandmother made, or ring your mum, or whoever was home to you. With a partner you'll want closeness and small rituals, the same cup of tea at the same hour. Dreams might be full of houses and old places. Let someone look after you for one evening, all of it, the meal and the washing up, and don't apologise for it.
moon.reversed:
Everything floods at once on a Cancer Moon. Small hurts feel huge, the past turns up uninvited, and you might find yourself crying over something from years ago as if it happened on Tuesday. Or it all goes inward, the door shuts, you go quiet for days and wait to see if anyone notices. Moodiness here is nearly always hurt that hasn't been said.

With family, old roles come back fast, the one who looks after everybody or the one who's always a bit let down. In the body it tends to sit in the stomach and in broken sleep. Pick one small practical thing to look after, a plant, the fridge, a drawer, and do it slowly. It gives the feeling somewhere to go that isn't the people you love.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising comes into a room carefully, checks who's there, and softens once it feels safe. With this card as the mask, the softening happens much faster than usual. People meet a warmth that seems to be offered on the spot, and they tend to open up to you, sometimes more than you were ready for. Cancer sits inside the card's own zone, so nothing needs translating, and with the Moon as your chart ruler you're very tuned to whoever's in front of you.

Across the chart, Capricorn holds your seventh house, and it's earth, which gets on well with water. You tend to pair up with people who look composed and a bit armoured, and the card shows you coming toward them with the tender side out. That works better than you'd expect, because people like that often need someone else to go first. The only catch is that your mask can make promises your moods can't always keep. You look endlessly available, and you aren't, and you need your quiet days.

In a new job you'll be the one everyone brings their troubles to by the end of the first month. On a date you'll seem sweet and slightly old-fashioned. With new neighbours or in-laws, you could be baking for them before you know their surname. Show the warmth, and keep a bit of your evening back for yourself.
rising.reversed:
Hurt shows on the surface with Cancer rising under this reversed Knight. People see you wince, go cool, take a joke personally. Or they get the overly sweet version, all niceness and no edges, which makes them faintly uneasy because they can tell something's going on underneath. The shell and the offered cup are both on show, and strangers can't work out which one to believe.

First days, first meetings and new groups bring it out, anywhere you don't feel safe yet. Around a partner's more serious friends, you might come across as moody when you're only nervous. Before you walk in, decide one thing you'll say about yourself, something small and real, and say it early. It lets people meet you, and it gives the nerves something to do.

sun.upright:
Leo loves a grand romantic gesture, and this is the card of one, so a Leo Sun tends to perk up when the Knight of Cups appears. Leo is fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, and you want to be seen for what you make and who you love, generously and in public. The Knight brings the rose, the song, the declaration under the window. The complication is the elements. Water and fire are opposed, and the card's feeling is the quiet, sincere sort that doesn't need an audience.

So you're pulled two ways. Part of you wants the gesture big enough that everyone hears about it, and another part wants it true enough that one person does. Oddly, it can feel like stage fright, because a real offer of the heart can be turned down and there's no applause to soften the landing. Strength is Leo's own Major, a woman resting her hand on a lion's jaw, and that sort of pride, the gentle kind, is the one that works here. I've seen Leo Suns do their best loving under this card and their worst showing off, sometimes in the same week.

In love it's a good card for courting someone properly, or for being courted and letting yourself enjoy it without making a speech. In creative work, whatever you make might be more personal than usual, and better for it. With children, if you have them or teach them, your warmth goes down very well. Do the romantic thing privately first, for one person, and notice how it feels with nobody watching.
sun.reversed:
Romance turns into theatre. The gestures get bigger and the feeling behind them gets thinner, and some part of a Leo Sun is watching to see how it's landing. If the response isn't what you'd hoped, pride takes over, and you sulk in a way that's quite loud for a sulk. Fire and water fighting here usually looks like drama, with you in the lead role.

In love it's the huge birthday surprise planned partly for the photos. At work it's creative output that's all style, or a flounce when feedback comes in. With friends you need a lot of reassurance and resent needing it. Pick one person and do something kind for them that nobody else will ever hear about. Don't post it, and don't mention it later.

moon.upright:
Being adored is what settles a Leo Moon, and there's no shame in it. You feel safe when you feel special to someone, when you're warmly noticed, and you hand that same warmth back by the bucketful. This Knight carries courtship in both hands. On your Moon he usually brings a longing to be romanced properly, or a strong urge to romance someone yourself. Water and fire are opposed, though, so the mood can boil over.

Leo is fixed, and these feelings don't pass quickly. Once you feel something you feel it for a good while, loyally, and the Knight's dreamy streak can have you building a whole love story around one kind look. It's lovely while it lasts. What you'll probably recognise is how exposed you feel waiting for someone to respond to your warmth, and how a small lack of response can hurt your pride far more than you'd let on.

With a partner, ask for the gesture you'd like, the date night, the flowers, whatever it is for you. With children, or anything playful and creative, you'll feel lighter and more generous. Your body might crave colour and sun and long warm evenings. Let yourself be the one who's courted for once, and when it comes, just say thank you.
moon.reversed:
The slightest thing can leave a Leo Moon feeling unloved under this reversed card. A partner forgets something small, a friend doesn't comment on the photo, and the hurt goes straight to your pride and settles in. You might sulk grandly, or go cold and wait to be won back. There's often some jealousy in it too, watching who else is getting the attention you wanted.

With a partner, it's the evening you both spend waiting for the other to apologise. With children or friends, it can come out as needing affection shown on your terms. Tell one person, plainly and without any drama, that you'd like some warmth from them. People who love you tend to respond to being asked far better than you expect.

rising.upright:
Leo rising walks in like the sun's come out. Warm, bright, a proper presence, with the Sun ruling your chart and your hair usually doing something impressive. Add this Knight and the entrance turns romantic. You come across as generous and a little dreamy, the sort who remembers names and makes people feel singled out, and a fair few will fall for you slightly on first meeting.

There's friction underneath. The card's water on your fire can soften you into someone gentler than usual, which some people love and you might find unsettling. Aquarius is opposite you, on the seventh, an air sign, cool and independent, so you're often drawn to people who keep a bit of distance. As a Leo rising with this card you may find yourself courting someone who needs time to warm up, and you'll want to push. Don't. Fire and water are already making enough steam between them.

In meetings and presentations you'll win people over by visibly caring about what you're presenting. At parties you'll be the one people queue up to talk to. On a date you'll make an ordinary evening feel like an occasion. Let a quieter person have the spotlight for a while, and notice how much they like you for it.
rising.reversed:
The charm can look performed. You come in big and romantic and people sense they're watching a show. Or the water dampens the fire and you arrive flat and a little wounded, quieter than anyone expects from a Leo rising, and they wonder what's wrong. Either way the first impression isn't quite you. It's often nerves, to be honest, and on this rising nerves come out as volume.

It tends to show early in dating, where flirting becomes a bid for attention, and at work, where you might oversell yourself in an interview. With new friends you could come on strong and then feel stung when they don't match it. Aim smaller. Walk in, say hello warmly, and let them come to you.

sun.upright:
Pisces is the sign opposite Virgo, and there's a lot of Pisces in this Knight, the dreaming, the idealism, the offer made on faith. So for a Virgo Sun the card brings in something from the far side of your own chart. Virgo is mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, and you define yourself by being useful, getting things right, the work of your hands and your head. Water and earth get on well, which helps. The Knight's feeling gives your practical side something worth doing, and your practical side gives the feeling some legs.

What you'll feel is the gap between the ideal and the real, and that's familiar ground. You're an idealist too. You just call it standards. Where the Knight rides straight after a dream, you'd normally inspect it first, and this card asks you to go along with the feeling a little way before the checking starts. The Hermit is Virgo's own Major, an old man alone on a mountain with his lamp, and this Knight is heading out to meet someone. That might be the stretch for you, honestly, letting yourself be met.

At work it's a good card for a project that means something to you, where the care and the skill go in together. In love it might mean letting someone see the soft, slightly fussy way you look after them, and letting them call it love. For the body, gentle movement and time near water tend to help. Let the first draft of something go out imperfect, a letter, a plan, a piece of work.
sun.reversed:
The inspector takes over. A lovely offer comes along and a Virgo Sun picks it apart until there's nothing left to accept. Or the quieter version, where you drift into daydreams about the perfect job or the perfect partner and let the real work and the real person slip, because neither will ever match what's in your head.

It shows at work in the project you won't hand in, and at home in the small criticisms a partner has started to flinch at. Worry might get into your stomach or your sleep. Mercury, your ruler, is very good at finding faults, and it doesn't switch off just because something is lovely. List what's genuinely wrong with the thing you're doubting, on paper, and then list what's good about it. Usually the second list is longer, and you can act from there.

moon.upright:
Feelings are safer for a Virgo Moon once they've been put somewhere. You need order to feel calm, a tidy kitchen, a plan for the week, a job to do for someone, and you often show love by fixing things. This Knight brings a feeling that won't fit in a drawer, soft and romantic and a little unreasonable. Earth and water are friendly, so it doesn't knock you flat, though it does get in under the routine.

It tends to feel like tenderness you don't quite know how to express. You want to look after someone, and without saying so you make them a cup of tea, pick up their dry cleaning, remember the thing they mentioned three weeks ago. That's a real language of love. With this card, though, some of the feeling wants to come out in words as well, and that's harder for a Virgo Moon, who'd sooner check the feeling is reasonable before admitting to it.

Your gut might settle when you're around someone who makes you feel safe, and churn when you're not. With a partner, small acts of care become the romance. In your work you may be drawn to something that helps people directly, with your hands. Tell one person, in plain words, one thing you love about them. You can make the tea as well.
moon.reversed:
Worry gets into love. You reread the message, analyse the tone, notice the small change in how someone said goodnight, and build an anxiety out of it. A Virgo Moon can also go the other way and hide in fantasy, a crush on someone safely out of reach who can't let you down, because the real person in front of you has flaws you can't stop seeing.

It usually shows in the body first, a tight stomach, broken sleep, eating too much or forgetting to. With a partner it comes out as picking at small things. When the worry starts, do something with your hands for half an hour, cooking, weeding, sorting a cupboard, and look at the feeling again afterwards. It'll often have shrunk to its real size.

rising.upright:
Neat, careful, observant, the person who notices the crooked picture frame and doesn't mention it. That's Virgo rising, with Mercury ruling the chart, and you usually lead with a sensible question. Draw the Knight for the way you meet people and a romantic softness comes through the tidiness. Strangers see a gentleness they might not have expected. Earth and water are friendly, so it suits you better than you'd think.

With this rising, Pisces falls on your descendant, the cusp of the seventh house, and Pisces is one of the water signs the card is drawn from. That's worth knowing. You're often drawn to dreamers, artists, people who live a bit inside their feelings, and the Knight on your front means you're showing some of that same quality yourself. It can make first meetings with those people much easier. It can also make you look very available when you don't feel it, and Virgo rising doesn't like being seen before it's ready.

Interviewers will see someone who cares about the work, which is useful. On a first date you'll seem kind and thoughtful and slightly shy. Your style might soften, a colour or a fabric you'd normally pass over. Let the softness show without explaining it.
rising.reversed:
Nerves make the charm stiff on Virgo rising. You want to come across warm and it comes out over-polite or anxious to please, apologising for things that aren't your fault, offering help nobody asked for. Or you're so careful not to seem soft that people read you as cold. Your hands give you away, fiddling with a cuff or a cup.

It shows at the start of things, a new job, meeting a partner's friends, the first few messages with someone you like. With Pisces opposite, it can draw people who need rescuing, and you'll be tempted. Say one thing about yourself that isn't useful or helpful, just something you like, and let people meet that part of you first.

sun.upright:
A Libra Sun already knows how to be courted, and how to court. Libra is cardinal air, ruled by Venus, and you build your sense of yourself through relationship, through beauty, through getting the balance right between people. The Knight of Cups is the card of the romantic offer, so it goes straight to the part of you that most wants to be one of a pair. Air and water sit neutral to each other, which means the card's feelings have to be put into words before you can really work with them.

The tension is in the scales. Justice is Libra's own Major, and Justice weighs things. The Knight doesn't weigh anything. He just rides toward what he loves. So you may find yourself wanting to follow a feeling and also wanting to be sure it's fair and sensible and good for everyone, and sometimes all that careful weighing lets the moment go by. I've seen a lot of Libra Suns who are wonderful at romance and very slow at actually choosing.

In love, a proposal or a real step forward may be on the table, or you may want to make one. In creative work, especially design, music, anything to do with how things look and sound, it's a lovely card for making something just because it's beautiful. Socially you'll be in demand. Make one choice with your heart and stick with it long enough to see what it becomes.
sun.reversed:
Being in love with being in love is the classic reversed Knight, and a Libra Sun is especially prone to it. You fall for the idea of someone, or the idea of yourself in a couple, and the actual person comes second. Or you can't choose, so you keep two possibilities going and tell yourself it's being fair. Charm does a lot of work here, smoothing over things that need saying.

In relationships it shows as avoidance, the difficult conversation postponed with a nice dinner. At work it's saying yes to everyone and then quietly resenting it. Choose one thing you've been sitting on the fence about and say plainly where you stand. People might be disappointed for a day, and then they'll know where they are with you.

moon.upright:
Peace is what a Libra Moon needs, peace between you and the people you love, a pleasant room, no harsh words. You feel settled when things are fair and nice to look at. This Knight brings a romantic mood into that, a yearning for closeness and for someone to share beautiful things with. Water and air are neutral elements, so the card's feeling doesn't just flow in. You feel it, and then you want to talk about it, share it, check it with somebody.

What you might recognise is a longing that's pleasant and a bit restless at once. You want romance, the candlelit kind, and you might be lonelier than you've told anyone, even while you're surrounded by people. Venus rules Libra, which makes your Moon very sensitive to atmosphere. A beautiful evening can lift you right up. A cold tone in someone's voice can put you off your dinner. This Knight makes both of those stronger.

At home you might want to make the place lovelier, candles, flowers, the furniture moved around. With a partner you'll want to be courted with a bit of ceremony. With friends, you'll be the one organising the nice dinner. Say what you'd like from someone out loud, even if it risks a small disagreement, and see whether the peace holds. It usually does.
moon.reversed:
Resentment can hide under the pleasantness. Something's wrong between a Libra Moon and someone close, and you smile, keep things nice, and let the feeling go sour somewhere out of sight. Or you soothe the loneliness with fantasy, imagining a different partner or a different life, one where nobody ever disagrees.

It usually shows in a relationship first, a coolness nobody's named. It can show in your social life too, saying yes to every invitation so you don't have to be alone with the mood. Sleep can go light, with the conversation you didn't have running on a loop. Have the small, honest conversation you've been avoiding, the one about the dishes or the tone or the weekend plans. It'll be less awful than you think, and the air will clear.

rising.upright:
Charming, attractive, easy to be around. That's Libra rising on an ordinary day, with Venus ruling the chart and a knack for making people comfortable. The Knight of Cups turns that up a long way. You come across as romantic and gracious, the sort of person who seems genuinely delighted to meet everyone, and plenty of people will go home thinking you fancied them.

Across from you is Aries, the sign on your descendant, and it's fire, which water fights with. So you're often drawn to people who are direct, bold and a bit impatient, and with this card you're meeting them in the softest way possible. That can be lovely. It can also cause misunderstandings, because the bold types want a clear yes or no and you're offering something beautiful and ambiguous. Your element and the card's don't clash, though they don't blend without effort either.

In client work and anything public-facing, people will love you. On dates, you'll be very good company and possibly hard to read. New friends will feel special around you. At a wedding you'll end up dancing with the shy cousin and making their night. Be clear once in a while about what you actually mean, especially with the direct people. They'll appreciate it, and so will you.
rising.reversed:
The charm goes on autopilot. A Libra rising smiles, agrees, flatters, and people leave feeling good and knowing nothing about you. Or you give out mixed signals without meaning to, warm in the room and vague afterwards, and someone ends up confused or hurt.

It tends to show in dating, where people think there's more on offer than there is, and at work, where agreeing with everyone in the meeting means nobody knows what you think. Friendships can suffer too, the ones where you're always the pleasant one and never the one who needs something. With Aries opposite, a blunt person might call you on it. Let them. Give one honest opinion early in the next conversation, even a small one about the food, so people have something real to go on.

sun.upright:
Scorpio is fixed water, and the Knight is water on the move, so a Scorpio Sun meets this card in its own element. Your sign is squarely inside his territory. Mars rules Scorpio traditionally, Pluto in the modern reading, and your sense of yourself is built on depth, loyalty, intensity, going all the way in or not at all. Underneath the pretty manners, the Knight's devotion is exactly the Scorpio sort, and the same element amplifies what's already there.

So you'll feel it strongly. There may be one person or one project you're devoted to with an intensity that surprises even you. The friction comes from the fixed part. Fixed water holds still, deep and private, and this Knight carries his feeling out into the open, cup held out for anyone to see. You may feel an urge to declare something you'd normally keep sealed up, and the fear of being seen can be almost physical. Death is Scorpio's own Major, and you already know how to let things end. With this card the harder job is letting something start.

In love or intimacy, it's a good card for letting someone closer than you usually would. In creative work or research you might go deeper into something than anyone else would bother to. Around trust, an old wound could soften a little. Tell one person something true that you've kept to yourself.
sun.reversed:
This is where the Knight's charm can turn into seduction with a purpose. Feelings a Scorpio Sun isn't saying go underground and come out as control. Testing people. Jealousy. Reading every message for the hidden meaning. Or an obsession with someone from the past, turned over and over because letting it go feels like losing.

It shows in relationships where you give a lot and want to know exactly what you're getting back. At work it might be a grudge against whoever got the credit. It can show in sleep too, the replaying at three in the morning. Say the feeling out loud instead of steering the situation toward it. It's riskier, and it's how people get to meet the actual you.

moon.upright:
A Scorpio Moon feels everything at full depth and shows almost none of it. You need trust above everything, and you need to know the people close to you will stay when things get dark. The Knight brings a romantic, devoted feeling into water that's already deep, and Scorpio is one of the three signs he rides out of. Water on water amplifies, sometimes beautifully and sometimes further than you'd choose.

Longing, maybe, for a closeness that goes all the way down. Tenderness toward someone that feels almost too big to hold. Mars rules your sign traditionally, and there's a heat in your feelings that most water signs don't have, so this Knight's soft devotion can come out fierce and protective in you. You'll probably catch yourself watching someone closely, reading them, wanting to be sure before you let any of it show. At work you may care about a colleague's trouble more than you'd ever let them know.

In intimacy it can be a deep and good card, a stretch when being close feels safe enough to go further. Your dreams may be vivid and full of old faces. With family, a long-held silence might start to ease. Let one person see how much you care before you're completely sure they'll handle it well.
moon.reversed:
Brooding is the risk here. Hurt goes underground and stays there, getting heavier. A Scorpio Moon might test someone to see if they'll prove their love, go silent to see whether they notice, or replay an old betrayal until it feels fresh again. The longing is still there. It's just been turned into suspicion.

It shows in relationships as withholding, affection given and then taken away. It shows in sleep as dark dreams and restless nights. With family, old grudges can flare over nothing much. You know exactly how to make someone feel shut out, and it's worth noticing when you're doing it. Name the hurt to the person involved, in a few words, so they don't have to guess. After that it's usually lighter than it's been in weeks.

rising.upright:
People feel Scorpio rising before they know a thing about you. There's a stillness in how you look at people, an intensity, and Mars as your traditional chart ruler gives it an edge. Drawn here, the Knight softens that into something magnetic and romantic. People are drawn to you, and they feel you're really paying attention to them, which you usually are.

Taurus is on your seventh house with this rising, earth, which gets on well with water. You're drawn to steady, sensual, reliable people, and the card shows you coming toward them with an openness you don't usually allow at the start. Mostly that's a good thing. The tension is that Scorpio rising likes to keep something back, and this Knight puts the cup out in front of you where anyone can see it. You might feel more exposed than you like, and people may think you're offering more than you mean to.

First dates with you tend to go late. In negotiations or meetings, people will find you persuasive because you so plainly care. In a new group you'll draw one or two people close fast. Let someone see you smile properly on first meeting, the full smile, the one you usually save.
rising.reversed:
The charm can feel calculated to other people, even when it isn't. A Scorpio rising under this reversed card is magnetic and hard to read, and people can't tell whether they're being courted or assessed. Sometimes they're right to wonder. The allure gets used as strategy, drawing people in to find out what they want before you show anything yourself.

It shows in first dates that feel like interviews, and in meetings where you hold back your view until you know who's on your side. New people might find you intimidating. With Taurus across the chart, a steady person may simply lose interest in the mystery and go home. Say what you want early and simply, before you've fully worked out the room. It feels risky, and it makes people trust you faster.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius and this Knight are both on a quest, which is why the card can feel oddly familiar on a Sagittarius Sun. You're mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter, and you know yourself by what you're heading toward, the big idea, the trip, the truth you haven't found yet. The Knight rides toward something too, only his quest is for someone to give his heart to. Fire and water are opposites among the elements. So you both love the horizon, and you want very different things once you get there.

You'll feel that as an itch between freedom and feeling. Part of you wants to fall hard for something, a person, a cause, a place, and part of you is already checking where the exits are. Temperance is Sagittarius' own Major, and if you look at that card, it's an angel pouring water from one cup into another, mixing things that don't naturally mix. That's the skill this pairing asks of you, and you're better at it than you'd think. Mutable signs bend. You can let a feeling in without it closing the road.

In love you might find yourself romanced by someone from somewhere else, or doing the romancing on your travels. In study or belief, something may move you emotionally in a way ideas usually don't. At work, a project with some meaning behind it will hold you far longer than one that only pays well. Say yes to the thing that moves you, and give it a proper length of time before you judge it.
sun.reversed:
Charming everywhere and committed nowhere, that's the reversed Knight on a Sagittarius Sun. You fall in love with a place, a person, a plan, and you're gone before it can ask anything of you. Promises get made in high spirits and forgotten on the next adventure. Sometimes it's grander, a belief or a teacher or a cause you idealise until it lets you down.

In love it shows as restlessness, the relationship that starts to feel like a cage the moment it's real. At work it's the big project dropped when it stopped being exciting. With friends it's the reunion you organised and then didn't come to. Go back to one thing you rode away from and see it through to a proper end, whatever that turns out to be.

moon.upright:
Space is what a Sagittarius Moon needs to feel alright. Room to move, a trip on the horizon, a laugh, the freedom to change your mind. Jupiter rules Sagittarius and makes your feelings generous and hopeful, quick to find the bright side. This Knight brings in something softer and more wistful, and fire and water pull against each other, so the mood can feel strange on you. Tender, when you'd much prefer cheerful.

You might find yourself missing someone far away, or aching for a place you've been. You might get sentimental about something you believe in. The Sagittarius reflex is to cheer yourself up, crack a joke, book a trip, which does work sometimes, and sometimes it's a way of dodging the feeling. The card asks you to let the soft mood stay for a bit. Mutable signs recover fast, so you'll bounce back whatever you do, and you might learn something if you don't rush it.

With a friend or partner who lives far away, a heartfelt call could mean a great deal. Your body might want the outdoors, walking, swimming, somewhere with a wide view. Study or spiritual practice may move you more than usual. Put on the music that makes you homesick and let it do its work.
moon.reversed:
Running from feelings is the habit to watch. Something sad or tender comes up and a Sagittarius Moon is off, a new plan, a joke, a spontaneous weekend away, anything that isn't sitting with it. Or the longing turns into restlessness, a sense that the good life is happening somewhere else and you're missing it.

It shows in relationships as leaving the room, literally or otherwise, when things get emotional. With family, it can be the visit home you keep cutting short. Friends who want to talk about something real may find you've changed the subject before they've finished. In the body it's a need to keep moving. Next time a heavy feeling arrives, stay put for ten minutes. Don't book, don't text, don't joke. Let it be there. Then go for a walk, if you still want to.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising greets the world with open arms and a slightly too loud laugh. You come across as friendly, adventurous, honest to the point of bluntness, and Jupiter as your chart ruler gives you a generous way of meeting people. The Knight brings romance and a softer touch to that. People see a traveller with a poet's streak, someone warm and a bit wistful who probably has a story about a train in another country.

The friction between fire and water shows up as a softening of your bluntness. You might choose your words more carefully, or be moved in front of strangers when you'd usually laugh it off. Gemini is opposite you, on the seventh house, an air sign, quick and chatty, and you're drawn to clever, talkative people. With this card you come toward them with your heart showing, which may surprise them and you. Some of them won't know what to do with it at first.

When you're travelling you'll make friends with strangers easily, and they'll remember you. In teaching or any public work, your warmth will carry the message further. On dates you'll be an adventure. Let the softer side lead in one conversation you'd normally make a joke of.
rising.reversed:
Big promises are the problem. You meet someone, love them, suggest the road trip, and by the next week you've moved on. Strangers find a Sagittarius rising wonderfully warm and discover later that the warmth came with no forwarding address. Or your bluntness gets tangled up with the Knight's moodiness, and you say something tactless and then sulk because it didn't land.

It shows on holidays, at conferences, at the start of friendships, anywhere the first impression outruns what comes after. At work it's the pitch that sounded brilliant and had nothing behind it. With Gemini opposite, you'll draw people who remember exactly what you said. Promise less when you're excited. Wait a day and then offer what you're genuinely going to do.

sun.upright:
A Capricorn Sun isn't known for romance, though you're more of a romantic than people think, only a private one. Capricorn is cardinal earth, ruled by Saturn, and you build yourself through work, responsibility, the long climb. The Knight is soft and dreamy and follows his heart wherever it goes. Your element and the card's are friendly, earth and water, which is the good news. They give each other shape, and what's grown between them tends to hold.

So the card lands on your will as a question. What would you do if you followed a feeling, just this once, with no plan behind it? That can seem almost frivolous to a Capricorn, and it's also what keeps the ambition from drying out. The Devil is Capricorn's own Major, the card of what binds you, and sometimes what binds a Capricorn Sun is the belief that feeling has to be earned first. The Knight brings it anyway, unearned, and you may not quite trust it.

At work this might be a move toward something you actually love, or bringing more of yourself into what you already do. In love it's a good card for showing someone how seriously you care, in words as well as by being reliable. With family, you might soften toward a parent or a child. Book one thing in your diary that's purely for delight, and keep the appointment the way you'd keep a meeting.
sun.reversed:
Feelings get filed under unproductive. A lovely offer comes along and a Capricorn Sun turns it down because there's work to do, or judges someone's romantic gesture as naive and feels a bit superior about it. The other version is quieter, a private longing you won't admit to, for a different life, a creative path, a person, sitting there under all the achievement. Some Capricorns treat romance as one more thing to achieve, the right partner at the right age.

At work it shows as burnout that looks like dedication. In love, as reliability without tenderness. With family, as always being the dependable one and never the one who's looked after. Tell someone about the other life you sometimes imagine, even as a joke. Saying it out loud takes some of the weight off.

moon.upright:
Control is how a Capricorn Moon feels safe. You handle things, you cope, you'd rather be competent than comforted, and you probably learned early that you could only count on yourself. This Knight arrives with a cup held out, offering tenderness. Earth and water get on, so there's no real threat in it. Someone's being kind to you and you're not sure where to put it.

It might surprise you. A longing for closeness you normally keep well wrapped. A soft spot for someone that's hard to ignore. Saturn rules Capricorn, and Saturn hates being caught off guard, so you may find yourself trying to manage the feeling, schedule it, keep it at a sensible level. With this card it tends not to stay at a sensible level for long, and I'd let it. Most Capricorn Moons I've known could do with more practice at being soft in front of someone.

Notice where you hold tension, the shoulders, the jaw, and whether it eases when you let yourself feel something. With a partner or a close friend, you might manage to accept care without deflecting it. With a parent, especially a father or whoever was the stern one, something old could soften. Let someone help you with one practical thing you'd normally do alone.
moon.reversed:
Shutting the feeling down and working harder is the Capricorn Moon's habit under this reversed card. Something tender or sad comes up, and you answer an email. It's efficient, and it builds up. There can be a low melancholy underneath, a sense that nobody sees how much you carry, and you'd never say so. Sometimes it's a sentimental streak you're embarrassed by, hidden so well that the people you love never get to see it.

It shows in the body first, tight shoulders, a clenched jaw, sleep that doesn't rest you. With a partner it can come out as coolness, or impatience with their feelings. With family, as taking on too much. Once a day, stop for five minutes and ask yourself what you're feeling, and answer honestly, in one word. It's small, and it adds up.

rising.upright:
Capricorn rising comes across serious, capable, a bit reserved, the one who looks like they've already read the agenda. Saturn rules your chart, and people often guess you're older than you are. This card cracks that open a little. People catch a warmth under the composure, a gentleness, and it makes you much easier to approach. It's worth noticing who starts opening up to you.

With Capricorn rising, Cancer holds the seventh house, and Cancer is one of the water signs this Knight rides out from. So you're often drawn to tender, nurturing, emotional people, the ones who make a home wherever they go. With this card you're showing some of that same softness at your own front door. Water and earth get on, so it sits comfortably, even though you might feel a bit exposed. The people who've always found you a touch intimidating may suddenly find you easy.

At work, colleagues may see a side of you that makes them trust you more. On a first date you'll seem steady and sweet, which is a rare combination. With new neighbours or in-laws, you might be warmer than they expected. Let the warmth show in the first five minutes, and see how differently people respond.
rising.reversed:
Stiffness is what comes through. A Capricorn rising wants to seem warm and it comes out formal, or the charm gets used like a tool, pleasant in a way that's clearly about getting somewhere. People can feel the strategy underneath and keep their distance. Or you're so guarded that the kindness you actually feel never makes it as far as your face.

It shows in job interviews and networking, where you come across polished and a little cold. On dates, it's a slightly rehearsed quality that makes the other person nervous. With Cancer opposite, the tender types you're drawn to may read you as distant. Say one soft thing early in a meeting, a compliment, a real question about their day, and mean it.

sun.upright:
Aquarius loves humanity in general and can go a bit stiff when one person loves it in particular. That's the joke people make, and there's some truth in it. The Knight of Cups is the card of devotion to one person, one feeling, one beautiful thing. Aquarius is fixed air, ruled by Saturn traditionally and Uranus in the modern reading, and your sense of yourself comes from your ideas, your independence, the future you want to build with your friends. Water and air are neutral. They don't clash, they just need introducing.

You're an idealist, though, as much as the Knight is, and that's where the card finds its way in. The Star is Aquarius' own Major, a woman kneeling to pour water out under a sky full of stars, and the Knight is carrying water toward somebody too. You may find your ideals turning personal, a cause becoming a person, or a friend becoming more than a friend. That can be unsettling for a fixed sign that likes knowing where it stands.

In friendships, one might deepen in a way you didn't see coming. In creative or community work you'll feel moved and want to act on it. In love it's a card for letting someone into the part of you that's usually kept for your ideas. Tell one person that they matter to you, individually, by name.
sun.reversed:
Cool detachment is where this one goes. A feeling comes along and an Aquarius Sun analyses it, steps back, and turns it into a theory about relationships. Or you idealise someone from a safe distance, the person who isn't available, the online friendship you'd never risk meeting, because distance keeps it perfect. Being Saturn-ruled, you can make the distance look like principle.

In love it shows as being there in body and elsewhere in feeling. In friendships, as supporting everyone's cause and never telling anyone what's hurting. At work it can be a creative idea you love and won't share in case someone changes it. Let one feeling stay personal. Don't explain it or generalise it. Say, to one person, that you miss them or like them or need them.

moon.upright:
Space and friendship settle an Aquarius Moon. You need freedom, room to think, people who don't crowd your feelings, and you often understand your emotions best from a small distance. This Knight rides in close with his cup out. Air and water have no quarrel, so there's no clash as such, and it still isn't your natural way. You'll probably feel it as a romantic mood that's appealing and faintly embarrassing at once.

You might catch yourself being sentimental in a way you'd normally tease someone else for. Tearing up at a film, missing someone, wanting to hold hands. There's often a friend involved, someone who's always been firmly in the friend category, and you notice you'd like something warmer from them. Being fixed, you'll try to keep the feeling steady and under control, and it may not let you. That's alright. It's good for you to be a bit knocked off balance.

With friends, one relationship might get closer and more tender. With a partner, you may want romance alongside the easy companionship you usually settle for. Online, you might find yourself drawn to someone far away. Give the feeling a night in, no analysing, and tell one friend about it.
moon.reversed:
Hot and cold, mostly. An Aquarius Moon feels close to someone, then panics about losing its independence and retreats into a cool friendliness. Or you get caught up in a fantasy about someone unavailable, safe precisely because nothing can come of it. Sleep can go strange too, with busy dreams full of crowds.

It shows in relationships as distance at the exact moment someone needs you close. In friendships, it's turning up for everyone's crisis and hiding your own. With a partner, it can look like being busy every night they're free. In the body there's a restless, nervy feeling that's hard to settle. When you notice yourself pulling away, say so to the person, even just that you've gone a bit distant and it isn't them, and then stay in the room.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising strikes people as friendly, a bit different, and slightly hard to get close to. You meet the world with an open, curious manner and an instinct for keeping some distance. The Knight gives that a dreamy, romantic edge, and people might take you for an artist or an eccentric poet. Air meeting water is a neutral pairing, so the card's softness doesn't fight your coolness. It just has to be introduced.

Leo holds your seventh house, the sign opposite yours, and it's fire. Warm, expressive, generous people tend to catch your eye, the ones who like the stage, and fire and water are never easy together. So when you come toward them with this Knight's softness, it can make a bit of steam. They might love the romance and be puzzled by the distance that's still there underneath. You may find yourself more open than usual on first meeting and then need a whole day to yourself afterwards.

In groups and networks you'll be memorable. On dates you'll seem intriguing and a bit unusual. A friend of a friend might remember you for years after one conversation. In creative or technical work, people might be surprised by how much feeling you bring. Let people see what moves you, and tell them why.
rising.reversed:
Mixed signals are the trouble. An Aquarius rising is friendly and warm on first meeting, then oddly cool, and people aren't sure whether you liked them. Or you come across as quirky and romantic in a way that feels a bit put on, as if you're playing a character. Being fixed air, you don't always notice you've gone quiet on someone.

It shows at parties and in new groups, where you might be the most interesting person in the room and the hardest to reach. On dates, it's charm followed by a long silence. At work, clients may like you and not quite trust your follow-through. With Leo opposite, warm people can feel rebuffed. Send the follow-up message you'd normally let slide. It's a small thing, and it shows people you meant it.

sun.upright:
Of all the signs, Pisces is the one this Knight feels most at home with. It's mutable water, ruled by Jupiter traditionally and Neptune in modern astrology, and your sense of yourself is built on imagination, compassion, the knack of feeling what other people feel. Pisces is one of the three signs the card belongs to, and its dreaminess is the Knight's dreaminess. The same element amplifies, so everything that's good about you gets stronger, and everything that's tricky does too.

The Moon is Pisces' own Major, the card of dreams and illusions and the narrow path between them, and that's the ground this Knight is riding over. What you'll feel is a strong pull toward something beautiful, a person, a creative project, a spiritual path, and a wish to give yourself to it completely. Being mutable, you'll probably find ways to make room for it. The tension is that both Pisces and this Knight tend to love the idea of a thing a little past the thing itself, and you might not notice when you've drifted off into the idea.

In creative work it's a wonderful card for making something with real feeling in it. In love it's a card for a sincere romantic gesture. In spiritual practice you might feel very connected. Pick one of these and give it a concrete shape, a finished piece, a date, a regular practice, something with an edge you can touch.
sun.reversed:
Escapism is the risk. The dream is so much nicer than the real, so a Pisces Sun drifts into it, into fantasy, screens, one more episode, a relationship that exists mostly in your head. Or you're rescuing someone, pouring yourself into them, because saving someone feels like love and the love you'd like for yourself feels like too much to ask.

It shows in work as the project that never quite takes shape. In love, as idealising someone who isn't really there for you. Money can slip through your fingers too, spent on things that feel like comfort. Pick one small, real thing, a walk, a phone call, a finished task, and do it with your whole attention. Let that be enough for one day.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon soaks up everything, other people's moods, the atmosphere in a room, the sad thing on the news, and needs time alone to wring it all out. Jupiter traditionally rules Pisces and Neptune in the modern reading, and both make your feelings wide and porous. This Knight is water on water, riding straight out of your own sign, and he brings romance, longing, a tenderness that can be almost too much.

You might find yourself falling a little in love with everything, a song, a stranger's kindness, a memory from years ago. There's something lovely in it and also a risk, because the Knight is always riding toward something, and a Pisces Moon can feel that pull as homesickness for a place that doesn't exist. Being mutable, your moods might shift a lot through a single day, and that's fine as long as you know it's happening.

Sleep and dreams could be vivid, even meaningful. With a partner you'll want tenderness and closeness, a long lazy morning, music on low. In creative work, feeling will pour out easily. Spend some time near water, a swim, a bath, a walk by the sea, and then come back to the ground with something warm to eat.
moon.reversed:
Overwhelm is what comes. Everything gets into a Pisces Moon and nothing goes out, until you're swimming in feelings you can't name. You might drift into daydreams to escape, sleep too much, lose yourself in screens, or fall for someone who isn't good for you because they seem to need you. Other people's moods stick to you and you carry them home.

It shows in the body as tiredness and fog. In relationships, as confusion about where you end and they begin. At work, as missed deadlines and not knowing why. Music helps, and so does anything that uses your hands. Set one small boundary, a time you'll switch off your phone, a no you'll say, and keep it for a week. It'll feel strange for the first few days.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets the world softly, with a gentle, dreamy manner that makes people feel you understand them. You tend to take on the colour of whoever you're with, and Jupiter as your traditional chart ruler adds kindness to it. This Knight suits you almost too well, water on water, and Pisces is part of his home ground. People see you as romantic, artistic, a little otherworldly, the poet at the party.

Virgo takes your seventh house with this rising, an earth sign, practical and precise. Organised, grounded people who seem to have their lives in order are often your type, and water and earth are friendly. With this card you'll meet them with your most open-hearted side, which usually charms them. The catch is the doubling. Two lots of water turn the softness right up. You may come across as so soft and available that people project all sorts onto you, or expect you to be their dream.

Someone on a first date may go home half in love with you. In creative work, people will be drawn to your feeling. In a new job, colleagues will confide in you quickly. Keep one thing about yourself clear and firm in first meetings, an opinion, a boundary, a preference, and say it out loud.
rising.reversed:
Vagueness is the trouble. You drift into rooms, agree with everyone, and leave people with a lovely feeling and no idea who you are. Or a Pisces rising shape-shifts so much, becoming whatever the person in front of you seems to want, that you lose track of yourself by the end of the evening. Friends might notice you're a slightly different person with each of them.

It shows in dating as being swept up in someone else's story. At work, as saying yes and then not following through because you never really meant it. With Virgo opposite, you might attract critical people who want to fix you. Decide one thing you want before you walk into a room, and say it before you leave.

1.upright:
Your body, your face, the way you walk into a room and the way you start anything, that's first-house territory. With this Knight drawn there, you lead with feeling. People see someone softer and more romantic than usual, and you may notice it in yourself too, wanting to dress a bit more beautifully, move a bit more slowly, be kinder to strangers in queues.

The first house is angular, one of the four corners of the chart, so whatever lands here gets acted out where people can see it. Aries is its natural sign and Mars its natural ruler, both fire, and the Knight's water doesn't get on with fire at all. So there's steam. The house wants you to act, decisively and first. The card wants to approach at a walk with the heart held out. You might feel that as impatience with your own tenderness, or as a newer kind of courage, the kind that shows it cares before it knows it'll be answered. Mercury has its joy in this house, and that helps, because it means the words tend to come when you're starting something.

For the body, flowing movement suits this, swimming, yoga, long walks with no target. Your appearance might want a change, a softer look, a colour you'd normally avoid. With new beginnings, leading with warmth will open doors that pushing wouldn't. Start one thing by telling someone honestly how you feel about it.
1.reversed:
Performing feeling is the risk in the first house. The charm is switched on and the look is soft, and it doesn't quite match what's going on inside you. Or it goes the other way and you're moody and it shows on your face, so people pick up on it before you've said a word. New people may take you for sad when you're only tired.

Mars rules this house naturally and wants action, and this Knight upside down gives it moodiness instead. You'll see it in how you start things, full of feeling at the outset and then fizzling. In the body it can look like restlessness, or like quietly letting your own care slide. Choose one habit that's about looking after your body, a walk, a proper meal, an earlier night, and do it for yourself and nobody else.

2.upright:
Actual money lives in the second house, the balance in the account, the things you own, and the harder question of what you think you're worth. With the Knight of Cups here, feeling gets tangled up with value. You might be drawn to spend on beauty, art, a gift for someone, or you might find money coming in through something you love doing, a creative sideline, work that comes from the heart.

This house belongs naturally to Taurus and to Venus, and it's succedent, the kind of house that's about what you build up and hold onto. Water and earth are friendly, so there's a good fit here. Feelings can turn into something solid, slowly, the way savings do. The tension is the Knight's usual one. He's generous and romantic and not always practical, and in the money house that can mean an overgenerous gesture, or a purchase made on the strength of a feeling that's gone by the time the bill arrives.

With money itself, it's a good time to put some toward something that genuinely delights you, inside a budget you've set first. With self-worth, you may find it easier to value what you give emotionally, and to ask to be paid properly for creative work. Something beautiful might come your way as a possession, too, a gift or a find. Write down what you'd spend on if money were no object, and buy the smallest thing on the list.
2.reversed:
Spending to feel better is the classic trap. Beautiful things bought to fill an emotional gap, money lent to someone because you care about them and never seen again, a gift given to win someone back. Or the other side of the second house, undervaluing yourself, giving your creative work away for nothing because asking to be paid feels unromantic.

It shows on bank statements, in a wardrobe of things bought on a mood, and in how you talk about what you're worth. Venus rules this house, and Venus has expensive taste when it's sad. It's usually a sad afternoon that empties the account. Before any purchase made in a mood, sleep on it. Then name a fair price for your work and say it without apologising.

3.upright:
The third house holds the ordinary traffic of a life, words and messages, siblings, neighbours, the short trips and errands that fill a day. With this Knight here, everyday conversation gets warmer. You might send a love letter, or a long message to a friend you've drifted from, or have a surprisingly tender chat with a brother or sister in the car.

It's a cadent house, one that adjusts and processes, and it belongs to Gemini and Mercury. Water and air are neutral, so the Knight's feelings have to find their way into words, and that isn't automatic. The Moon has its joy here, though. That's an old idea, that the Moon is happiest in the third, and it means feelings get a proper hearing in this part of the chart. You might find you're able to say things you'd usually leave unsaid, and in a lighter way than you'd expect.

With siblings or cousins, a warm reconnection could happen. Study might pull you toward poetry, music, a language, anything that carries feeling. Short trips could turn romantic, a day at the beach, a drive somewhere lovely with the windows down. A neighbour you've only ever nodded to might turn out to be good company. Write to someone you've lost touch with, by hand if you can, and post it.
3.reversed:
Sweet words that don't mean much are the reversed Knight's habit among the messages and errands of the third house. Texts full of charm and no follow-through, promises made in passing, flirting that leaves people confused. Or it goes quiet, you can't find the words for what you feel, and people misread the silence. With water and air only neutral to each other, the feeling and the words keep missing each other.

With siblings, it can show as an old sentimental story that doesn't match what actually happened. Gossip can creep in too, a feeling told to the wrong person because it had to go somewhere. Keep your word on one small thing, the call you said you'd make, the recipe you promised your neighbour, and do it promptly.

4.upright:
Home, family, the roots of things, the private ground you come back to at the end of a day. With the Knight of Cups in the fourth house, feeling comes home. You might want to make the place more beautiful, ask someone to move in, reconnect with family, or find that home itself starts to feel romantic again after a long time of just being where you sleep.

The fourth is an angular house, the very bottom of the chart, and its natural sign is Cancer, ruled by the Moon. Cancer is one of this Knight's own signs, so the card is speaking the house's language, water on water, and that amplifies. Home feelings go deep and nostalgic and tender, and they can flood if you're not careful. Old family memories might come up, some sweet, some harder.
